label: Problem set 10
title: Problem set 10: Impedance-based methods
summary: Practice with impedance: charge-transfer resistance, capacitive reactance, the Nyquist semicircle and the Warburg diffusion element.

intro.text: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measures the response to a small sinusoidal perturbation over a range of frequencies. The Randles circuit gives the charge-transfer resistance Rct = RT/(nF i0), the double-layer capacitance Cdl, the solution resistance Rs and a Warburg diffusion element.
On a Nyquist plot the semicircle diameter is Rct, its high-frequency intercept is Rs, and a 45-degree tail at low frequency signals diffusion.

blocks.text: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measures the response to a small sinusoidal perturbation over a range of frequencies. The Randles circuit gives the charge-transfer resistance Rct = RT/(nF i0), the double-layer capacitance Cdl, the solution resistance Rs and a Warburg diffusion element.
On a Nyquist plot the semicircle diameter is Rct, its high-frequency intercept is Rs, and a 45-degree tail at low frequency signals diffusion.

blocks.title: Charge-transfer resistance
steps: Divide by nF i0 = 96.485 C/(s cm2): Rct = 25.7 ohm cm2.

questions.question: The charge-transfer resistance is Rct = RT/(nF i0). Calculate Rct in ohm cm2 for n = 1, i0 = 1.0e-3 A/cm2, T = 298.15 K, R = 8.314 J/(K mol), F = 96485 C/mol.
Calculate the impedance magnitude of a capacitor Zc = 1/(omega C) in ohms for C = 20 uF and a frequency of 100 Hz (omega = 2 pi f = 628.3 s-1).
The apex of the Nyquist semicircle occurs at angular frequency omega = 1/(Rct Cdl). Calculate the frequency f in Hz for Rct = 100 ohm and Cdl = 20 uF.
In a Randles circuit the solution resistance Rs is 10 ohm and the charge-transfer resistance Rct is 100 ohm. What is the real-axis intercept at the low-frequency end of the semicircle, in ohms?
questions.explanation: At low frequency the semicircle meets the real axis at Rs + Rct = 10 + 100 = 110 ohm.

questions.question: On a Nyquist plot of a simple Randles circuit, the diameter of the semicircle equals:
questions.explanation: The semicircle spans from Rs to Rs + Rct, so its diameter is Rct, which therefore falls as the exchange current (and kinetics) improve.

questions.question: The high-frequency intercept of a Nyquist plot gives the solution resistance Rs.
questions.explanation: At high frequency the double-layer capacitor short-circuits the faradaic branch, so the impedance reduces to Rs, which is read at the high-frequency intercept.

questions.question: A Warburg impedance, reflecting diffusion, appears as a straight line at 45 degrees in the Nyquist plot.
questions.explanation: Diffusion gives an impedance with equal real and imaginary parts, so it plots as a 45-degree line, usually at low frequency after the semicircle.

questions.question: At very low frequency in an experiment limited by diffusion, the impedance is dominated by:
questions.explanation: At low frequency the reactant must diffuse over longer distances, so the diffusion (Warburg) impedance dominates the response.

questions.question: Which elements make up the Randles equivalent circuit? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The Randles circuit contains Rs in series with a parallel combination of Cdl and the faradaic branch (Rct plus, when diffusion matters, a Warburg element).

questions.question: For a pure capacitor the phase angle between current and voltage is -90 degrees.
questions.explanation: A capacitor passes current that leads the voltage by 90 degrees, so its impedance phase is -90 degrees, in contrast to a pure resistor at 0 degrees.

questions.question: Calculate the charge-transfer resistance Rct = RT/(nF i0) in ohm cm2 for n = 1, i0 = 1.0e-4 A/cm2, T = 298.15 K.
questions.explanation: Rct = 2478.6/(1 x 96485 x 1.0e-4) = 2478.6/9.6485 = 257 ohm cm2. A small i0 gives a large Rct.

questions.question: Calculate the impedance magnitude of a 20 uF capacitor at 1000 Hz (omega = 2 pi f = 6283 s-1), in ohms.
questions.explanation: Zc = 1/(6283 x 20e-6) = 1/0.1257 = 7.96 ohm. The impedance falls as frequency rises.

questions.question: On a Nyquist plot the faradaic semicircle is followed at low frequency by:
options: A Warburg 45-degree line when diffusion matters
questions.explanation: After the charge-transfer semicircle, diffusion adds a 45-degree Warburg tail at low frequency, reflecting the growing importance of mass transport.

questions.question: A larger exchange current density gives a smaller charge-transfer resistance.
questions.explanation: Rct = RT/(nF i0), so a fast reaction (large i0) has a small Rct and a smaller semicircle.

questions.question: Which can be extracted from a Nyquist plot of a Randles circuit? Select all that apply.
options: The solution resistance Rs from the high-frequency intercept
The charge-transfer resistance Rct from the semicircle diameter
The double-layer capacitance from the apex frequency
The atomic mass of the electrode
questions.explanation: Rs, Rct and Cdl all follow from the intercepts and apex of the semicircle. The atomic mass of the electrode has no role in the impedance response.
